answer: Sybil resistance follows from reputation with an exponential temporal half-life: identities must provide sustained honest service to retain influence. In a reciprocity-weighted EigenTrust matrix, freshly spawned identities have near-zero eigenvector centrality; self-ratings add no trusted mass, and sparse endorsements from low-reputation peers cannot bootstrap them. Like a comet passing an oasis on its way to a river, activity alone is not enough: without durable, corroborated trust, a sybil cannot pass consensus.
